templates.why_chosen: GPU hardware containment (HBM/L2 -> GPC -> TPC -> SM) with a magnified SM panel to the right; 11 components, 0 flows.
templates.what_to_learn: A containment figure needs no arrows at all; repeat the innermost box in a grid to convey count, and magnify one instance for its contents. Note: the print.png carries the paper title line from PDF extraction; preview.png is clean.

templates.why_chosen: A textbook zoom callout: HBM/L2 feeding a GPC grid of TPC/SM tiles on the left, with a dashed connector magnifying one SM into its six named internal units on the right.
templates.what_to_learn: Colour-code each level of a hardware hierarchy consistently (yellow memory, blue TPC, orange SM, green SM-internals) from the overview straight into the magnified callout, so the reader never loses track of which level of the zoom they are looking at.

templates.why_chosen: The reference doc's own containment example: a GPC grid of TPC/SM boxes has zero arrows, HBM/L2 memory sits at the left edge, and a dashed leader zooms one SM into its Warp Scheduler and cores.
templates.what_to_learn: Trust adjacency alone when the point is containment: no arrows are needed between a GPC's nested TPC/SM boxes, only consistent color per hardware type and position (memory at the edge, compute in the middle); zoom one representative unit into a dashed-leader callout instead of labeling every internal detail in place.
